'''Ewald Rudolf Weibel''' [[FRMS|HonFRMS]] (5 March 1929 – 19 February 2019) was a Swiss anatomist and physiologist and former director of the Institute of Anatomy at the [[University of Bern]].  He was one of the first scientists to describe the endothelial organelles [[Weibel–Palade body|Weibel–Palade bodies]], which are named after him and his Romanian-American colleague [[George Emil Palade]].<ref>{{cite journal |author=Weibel ER, Palade GE |title=New cytoplasmic components in arterial endothelia |journal=J. Cell Biol. |volume=23 |issue= 1|pages=101–12 |date=October 1964 |pmid=14228505 |pmc=2106503 |doi=10.1083/jcb.23.1.101}}</ref> He was known for his work on the anatomy of gas exchange in lungs on multiple spatial scales using [[stereology]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ochs |first=Matthias |date=2020-09-01 |title="And then I met Ewald Weibel" |journal=American Journal of Physiology. Lung Cellular and Molecular Physiology |language=en |volume=319 |issue=3 |pages=L403–L407 |doi=10.1152/ajplung.00313.2020 |pmid=32640838 |s2cid=220439564 |issn=1040-0605|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Weibel |first=Ewald R. |date=2013-09-15 |title=A retrospective of lung morphometry: from 1963 to present |url=https://www.physiology.org/doi/10.1152/ajplung.00169.2013 |journal=American Journal of Physiology. Lung Cellular and Molecular Physiology |language=en |volume=305 |issue=6 |pages=L405–L408 |doi=10.1152/ajplung.00169.2013 |pmid=23851316 |issn=1040-0605|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Weibel was born in [[Buchs, Aargau|Buchs]] in the [[Aargau]] canton of Switzerland. After studying medicine at the [[University of Zurich]] (state examination 1955, Dr. med. 1956), he spent several years studying in the US at [[Yale University]] in New Haven, as well as at [[Columbia University]] and the [[Rockefeller University|Rockefeller Institute]] (now Rockefeller University) in New York, most recently as a career Investigator for the Health Research Council of the City of New York. In 1963 he returned to the Anatomical Institute of the University of Zurich as an assistant professor and in 1966 he was appointed full professor and director of the Anatomical Institute at the [[University of Bern]] until his retirement in 1994. He was Rector of the [[University of Bern]] from 1984 to 1985. From 1979 until 1996 he was Visiting Agassiz Professor and Associate in the Museum of Comparative Zoology at [[Harvard University]]. After his retirement, he was vice president and Secretary of the Maurice E. Müller Foundation for Orthopedic Surgery until 2000. He was founding president of the Union of Swiss Societies for Experimental Biology (1969–1972), President of the Swiss Academy of Medical Sciences (1996–2000) and President of the International Union of Physiological Sciences (1997–2001).<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hoppeler |first1=Hans |last2=Lindstedt |first2=Stan L. |date=2019-05-01 |title=Ewald R. Weibel (1929–2019) |journal=Journal of Experimental Biology |volume=222 |issue=9 |article-number=jeb205260 |doi=10.1242/jeb.205260 |pmid=31048402 |bibcode=2019JExpB.222B5260H |s2cid=143432192 |issn=1477-9145|doi-access=free }}</ref>

His scientific work covered four main areas: the morphometry of the human lung as the structural basis of the gas exchange function; the development of morphometric and stereological methods; the application of these methods in cell biology to measure the membrane system of the liver cell and the mitochondria in the muscles; integrative studies in comparative physiology, particularly on the question of the optimal structural basis of the organismic functions of the respiratory system, from the lungs to the muscle cells and their mitochondria, based on the hypothesis of [[symmorphosis]]. The discovery of the [[Weibel-Palade bodies]] in 1962 was an accidental observation. Ewald Weibel was married to the violinist and musicologist Verena Weibel-Trachsler.

== Honors and awards ==
Weibel was awarded numerous awards and accolades in life, a selected list is in the following.
* 1974: [[Marcel Benoist Prize]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://marcel-benoist.ch/en/current-laureate/past-laureates/|title=Marcel Benoist Prize: past laureates|access-date=31 October 2017}}</ref>
* 1979: Honorary Fellow of the [[Royal Microscopical Society]]
* 1979: [[Felix Fleischner]] Medal
* 1981: Foreign Associate of the [[U.S. National Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amacad.org/peerCollaboration/profile.aspx?c=psa&q=Weibel|title=Professor Ewald Rudolf Weibel|work=American Academy of Arts and Sciences|access-date=31 October 2017|archive-date=7 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107023730/https://www.amacad.org/peerCollaboration/profile.aspx?c=psa&q=Weibel|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 1982: College Medalist, [[American College of Chest Physicians]]
* 1985: Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]
* 1987: [[Anders Retzius]] Gold Medal, Karolinska Institutet, Stockholm
* 1987: Member of the [[Royal Society of Sciences in Uppsala]]
* 1988: H.R. Schinz Medal, Swiss Society of Radiology<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-04-21 |title=Schinz-Medaille |url=https://sgr-ssr.ch/schinz-medaille/ |access-date=2022-12-22 |website=Schweizerische Gesellschaft für Radiologie |language=de-DE}}</ref>
* 1988: Honorary Degree of Doctor of Science, [[University of Edinburgh]]
* 1988: Member of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]]
* 1989: Member of the [[German Academy of Natural Scientists Leopoldina]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.leopoldina.org/fileadmin/redaktion/Mitglieder/CV_Weibel_Ewald_R_D.pdf|work=Leopoldina Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften|title=Curriculum Vitae Prof. Ewald R. Weibel|access-date=31 October 2017|language=de}}</ref>
* 1992: Individual member of the Swiss Academy of Medical Sciences
* 1993: [[Jan Evangelista Purkyně|Jan Evangelista Purkinje]] Gold Medal, Prague
* 1998: Member of the [[Academia Europaea]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Academy of Europe: Weibel Ewald |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Weibel_Ewald |access-date=2022-12-22 |website=www.ae-info.org}}</ref>
* 1999: Honorary Doctor of Medicine, [[University of Geneva]]
* 1999: Honorary Foreign Member, [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]
* 2000: Honorary member of the [[Swiss Academy of Sciences]]
* 2004: Honorary member of the Swiss Academy of Medical Sciences
* 2005: Prix La Recherche with [[Bernard Sapoval]] & [[Marcel Filoche]], Paris
* 2007: Educational Award, [[European Respiratory Society]]
